title: Streaming usage-events harmonizer for per-tenant normalization
creator: Aisha Kapoor
description: Problem: telemetry emitted by Console frontends and agents comes in inconsistent shapes (route-level, user-level, legacy SDK envelopes). This makes downstream aggregation expensive and causes duplicative joins in the real-time pipeline, increasing cost and tail latency for per-tenant dashboards. Goal: build a lightweight streaming harmonizer stage that normalizes incoming usage events into a compact canonical envelope and emits tenant-aware, SLO-tagged records for downstream aggregators and alerting rules. The harmonizer must run with bounded state, support exactly-once semantics for idempotent fields, and preserve high-cardinality tags without exploding cardinality in the metrics storage.
proposal: Introduce a stateless-enrichment + bounded-state normalization operator upstream of the existing shard router. Key features: 1) schema inference for legacy envelopes with a deterministic ordering for fields, 2) tenant extraction and canonical tenant_id output, 3) event type canonicalization (map legacy names to v2 taxonomy), 4) minimal KV for deduplication of inflight event IDs (configurable TTL), 5) SLO tags added based on route and priority headers. Operator will be implemented as a lightweight Rust service running as an autoscaled K8s deployment, with Kafka / Pulsar connectors for input and output topics. We will avoid full reprocessing by emitting a compact change-log event when schema normalization changes occur.
tradeoffs_and_risks: Adding another stage increases end-to-end latency; mitigate via narrow protobuf payloads and CPU-optimized runtime
Deduplication requires bounded state and careful TTL tuning to avoid memory pressure
Canonicalization may hide original fields required by some downstream jobs — we will include original_raw pointer as optional field and preserve raw in cold storage
Rolling out to all tenants risks regressions; use canary tenants and split streaming topics by environment
implementation_notes: Use existing tenant extraction library from ENG-67211 to keep logic consistent
Expose a small HTTP /health and /metrics endpoint; integrate with console observability
Provide config-driven mapping tables for legacy->v2 event names, stored in ConfigMap with SHA-based reloads
Dedup TTL default 1 hour, pluggable per-namespace by config
updates: 2025-02-12: Spike completed. Validated normalization approach with 50k events/s replay of staging sample; peak CPU 60% on 8vCPU pod.
2025-02-20: Design review with PM and Design. Agreed to include original_raw pointer and to preserve user-level id when present.
2025-02-27: Prototype written in Rust. Benchmark: 200k events/s on r5.4xlarge equivalent with protobuf compacting; end-to-end p95 added ~12ms.
2025-03-03: Security review checklist drafted. Decided not to persist PII fields; map user identifiers to tenant-scoped hashes in harmonizer.
2025-03-05: Integration test with shard router passing; started canary deployment to staging-tenants topic

Add feature flag and rollout plan for 10% of tenants then 100%

Add automated schema-change alerting and rollback hook

Property tests for dedup semantics under reordering
